mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, if there’s one thing to take with you from this journey, it’s that art is never really done. It’s always moving, always shifting—reacting to the world around us, and to whatever’s happening inside us. Living with the shock of the new isn’t about a single moment. It’s a way of seeing, of staying open to change, asking questions, and having the courage to picture something different. Think about what the story of modern art really means for your own life: Change is always happening—and creativity? That’s how we find our way through it. Art lives and breathes through questions, not just answers or old traditions. Every voice matters. Art gets richer when more stories are told. Sure, technology connects us, but real connection needs care—real attention. And those lines between art and life? They’re always moving—so don’t stop being curious. Here’s the thing: you don’t have to be a painter or a poet to live with that sense of newness. Every day brings its own mix of challenges, confusions, and possibilities. The artists we’ve talked about remind us—it’s okay to feel lost sometimes, to question, to start over. They show us that there’s beauty in the unexpected, that meaning can spring up from chaos, and that hope is always worth holding onto. So, as you face the surprises and shocks of your own time, keep your mind open. Notice what’s around you. Listen deeply. And don’t be afraid to make your own mark. The world keeps changing—and you’re part of its story.
